target_customer: Consumers, first aimed at millennial women and then all adults, paying per session or subscription for online counseling, coaching and meditation instruction
problem: Traditional therapy is hard to access because of insurance gridlock, referral friction, long waits and cost. The company offered licensed counselors and coaches by video, written journal and text.
business_model: Marketplace for online counseling and coaching sessions, consumer pay per session or plan

founders.name: Bea Arthur
prior_employers: Amazon (built mental health platforms, per YC page)
MetLife (built mental health platforms, per YC page)
education: Columbia University, trained psychotherapist (LMHC), per YC page
previous_startups: Pretty Padded Room (online therapy site, the pilot that became In Your Corner)
founders.background_notes: Pitched Pretty Padded Room on Shark Tank in an episode aired February 2013 and received no deal, per Shark Tank Blog.

founders.name: Anthony Garcia
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO with no bio. Technical status inferred from the CTO title only.

exit.reason: Shark Tank Blog says the business shut down in 2016. A search snippet quotes Arthur in a 2022 interview attributing the closure to technical debt that became personal debt (not opened in full).

competitors.name: Talkspace
competitors.what: Unlimited text messaging therapy with licensed therapists
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the source snippet
competitors.funding_then: Raised $2.5M from Spark Capital and SoftBank Capital in May 2014

technical_complexity.rationale: Video, text and journal sessions plus HIPAA compliant accounts were standard web engineering in 2014. The YC description also mentions a planned mobile app. No unusual research problem was involved.

defensibility.rationale: Counselor supply was curated but not exclusive, and Talkspace was already funded in the same space. The only differentiator named was brand and gender inclusive positioning.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Talkspace kept growing and later became a large public player. No incumbent bought or copied In Your Corner; it closed in 2016 per Shark Tank Blog.

market_need_then: The YC description cites insurance gridlock, referral friction, wait times and cost. Talkspace raising money in May 2014 shows investor interest in online therapy that year. The founder's earlier Shark Tank pitch reported 21,000 dollars in year to date sales at taping (Shark Tank Blog), which suggests modest demand for the original site.

identity.visual_style: Described by YC as an aspirational brand for counseling, coaching and calm
identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive and gender inclusive, a deliberate shift from the earlier Pretty Padded Room name

rebrands.why: YC page says the new brand is more gender inclusive and convenient and broadens beyond counseling to coaching. No source states the founder's own reason beyond that.

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of merch, memes or fan community found. Press about the founder (Shark Tank, Bustle) covered the earlier brand more than In Your Corner.

brand_strength.rationale: The rebrand was a conscious move away from a name some commenters called offensive (Shark Tank Blog comments), but no source shows the new brand drove awareness or growth. The old site later redirected to 7 Cups.

pivots.from: Pretty Padded Room, online therapy site for millennial women
pivots.to: In Your Corner, gender inclusive counseling and coaching marketplace with a planned mobile app
pivots.why: Broaden the audience and add coaches and meditation instructors, per the YC description

outcome_analysis: In Your Corner relaunched the founder's earlier Pretty Padded Room site in 2014 with a broader brand and a YC place, but no priced funding round could be found and the company shut down in 2016. Secondhand accounts in search snippets say funding ran out in 2015 and the founder took revenue based loans, and the founder later pointed to technical debt. The earlier Shark Tank pitch showed small sales and no deal. The tags above reflect these partial sources, and the exact cause is not confirmed by a primary document.
notes: No company website listed on YC. Search snippets (not opened) say Arthur reported funding ran out around May 2015 and that she used merchant loans; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Crunchbase page for Pretty Padded Room showed only placeholder text. Whether Shark Tank related outside money came in is only a snippet claim. failure_factors weak_willingness_to_pay is a judgment from small pilot sales, not stated by a source.
